title: Government and the law in Australia

questions.q: What is the supreme law of Australia by which government must abide?
When did Australian Constitution come into effect?
How many levels of government in Australia?
Who is the Head of State of Australia under constitutional monarchy?
questions.a: The King of Australia (King of UK as King of Australia)

questions.q: Who represents the King in Australia?
Who represents the King in each state?
What are the two houses of Federal Parliament?
Where does Federal Parliament meet?
What is the role of the High Court?
questions.a: Interprets and applies the law, including Constitution

questions.q: Who is the head of the Australian Government?
How is the Prime Minister chosen?
questions.a: Leader of party with majority in House of Representatives

questions.q: What is a referendum?
questions.a: Vote by all voters on change to Constitution

questions.q: What is compulsory for Australian citizens aged 18 and over?
questions.a: Enrol and vote in federal and state elections

questions.q: What is the secret ballot?
questions.a: People vote privately, no one can influence how they vote
w: Everyone must show how they voted

questions.q: What is on the electoral roll?
questions.a: List of people registered to vote

questions.q: Who enforces the law and keeps peace?
What is jury service?
questions.a: Citizens decide if person is guilty or not guilty

questions.q: What should you do if you see a crime or know someone is planning a serious crime?
w: Take the law into your own hands
questions.e: If people suspect someone may be planning a serious crime, they should report it to the authorities as soon as possible, to help keep the community safe.

questions.q: Australia is a constitutional monarchy. What does this mean?
questions.a: King is Head of State whose powers limited by Constitution

questions.q: Which government is responsible for hospitals and schools?
Which government is responsible for passports and defence?
Which government is responsible for local roads and rubbish collection?
What is the role of local government?
questions.a: Local services like parks, libraries, rubbish

questions.q: How often are federal elections held?
What does coalition mean?
questions.a: Joining of two or more political parties to form government

questions.q: What is the minimum age to stand for Federal Parliament?
Is voting by secret ballot in Australia?
What is the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) responsible for?
questions.a: Manages tax and superannuation to fund services

questions.q: What is Services Australia?
questions.a: Delivers health, social, welfare payments via Medicare, Centrelink

questions.q: Who are eligible to be Governor-General?
questions.a: Appointed by King on advice of PM

questions.q: What does Governor-General do?
questions.a: Signs Bills into law, performs ceremonial duties

questions.q: What is the role of Senate?
Why does the Australian Constitution divide the power of government between Parliament, the Executive and the judges?
questions.a: To stop one person or group from holding all the power
w: To give the Prime Minister all the power
So the courts can make all the laws
questions.e: The Constitution divides power between the legislative (Parliament), executive and judicial (judges) powers, to stop one person or one group from holding all the power.

questions.q: Who has the power to make and change laws in Australia?
questions.e: Legislative power is the power to make laws. Parliament has the power to make and change the laws in Australia.

questions.q: How many senators does each state elect?
questions.e: Each state elects 12 senators, and the ACT and Northern Territory elect two each, a total of 76 senators.

questions.q: After a federal election, who forms the Opposition?
questions.a: The party or coalition with the second largest number of members in the House of Representatives
w: The party with the most members in the Senate
The judges of the High Court
questions.e: The party or coalition with the second largest number of members in the House of Representatives forms the Opposition. Its leader is the Leader of the Opposition.
